question.:question/problem:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by the closed curve $C$ with positive orientation and parametrization $r(t)=\langle 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}, - 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}, 1\rangle$ for $t\in [0,2 \pi).$
Given that $F(x,y,z)=\langle 3 y, - 3 x, 0\rangle,$ evaluate the integral

$$
\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm{d}S.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $S$ be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth boundary $C$ with positive orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $S,$ then Stokes' theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=2 \cos{\left(t \right)},\quad y=- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)},\quad z=1
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\langle 3 y, - 3 x, 0\rangle \\ & =\langle 3 \left(- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right), - 3 \left(2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right), 0\rangle \\ & =\langle - 6 \sin{\left(t \right)}, - 6 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r\prime(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(1\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle - 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}, - 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t) & =\langle - 6 \sin{\left(t \right)}, - 6 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\cdot \langle - 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}, - 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle \\ & =\left(- 6 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 6 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(- 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right)\cdot \left(0\right) \\ & =\left(12 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(12 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right) \\ & =12 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 12 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} \\ & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm dS & =\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi} F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\left(12\right)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\left[\left(12 t\right)\right]_{0}^{2 \pi} \\ & =\left(\left(24 \pi\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right)\right) \\ & =24 \pi\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:

$$
\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm{d}S.
$$

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∬}_{S}\text{curl}\,F\cdot \text{d}S.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=4 t^{3} - 4 t,\quad y=- 3 t^{2} - 3 t,\quad z=- 2 t^{2} - 2 t
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\langle y, 0, x\rangle \\ & =\langle \left(- 3 t^{2} - 3 t\right), 0, \left(4 t^{3} - 4 t\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle - 3 t^{2} - 3 t, 0, 4 t^{3} - 4 t\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r\prime(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(4 t^{3} - 4 t\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- 3 t^{2} - 3 t\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- 2 t^{2} - 2 t\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle 12 t^{2} - 4, - 6 t - 3, - 4 t - 2\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t) & =\langle - 3 t^{2} - 3 t, 0, 4 t^{3} - 4 t\rangle\cdot \langle 12 t^{2} - 4, - 6 t - 3, - 4 t - 2\rangle \\ & =\left(- 3 t^{2} - 3 t\right)\cdot \left(12 t^{2} - 4\right)+\left(0\right)\cdot \left(- 6 t - 3\right)+\left(4 t^{3} - 4 t\right)\cdot \left(- 4 t - 2\right) \\ & =\left(- 36 t^{4} - 36 t^{3} + 12 t^{2} + 12 t\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(- 16 t^{4} - 8 t^{3} + 16 t^{2} + 8 t\right) \\ & =- 52 t^{4} - 44 t^{3} + 28 t^{2} + 20 t \\ & =- 52 t^{4} - 44 t^{3} + 28 t^{2} + 20 t\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm dS & =\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr \\ & =\int_{-1}^{0} F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\int_{-1}^{0}\left(- 52 t^{4} - 44 t^{3} + 28 t^{2} + 20 t\right)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\left[\left(- \frac{52 t^{5}}{5}\right) + \left(- 11 t^{4}\right) + \left(10 t^{2}\right) + \left(\frac{28 t^{3}}{3}\right)\right]_{-1}^{0} \\ & =\left(\left(0\right) + \left(0\right) + \left(0\right) + \left(0\right)\right)-\left(\left(\frac{52}{5}\right) + \left(-11\right) + \left(10\right) + \left(- \frac{28}{3}\right)\right) \\ & =- \frac{1}{15}\end{aligned}
$$

x=2 \cos{\left(\pi t \right)},\quad y=- 2 \sin{\left(\pi t \right)},\quad z=- \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(2 \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- 2 \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle - 2 \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}, - 2 \pi \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}, \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\rangle\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t) & =\langle 6 \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}, 0, - 6 \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\rangle\cdot \langle - 2 \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}, - 2 \pi \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}, \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\rangle \\ & =\left(6 \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(- 2 \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right)\cdot \left(- 2 \pi \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)+\left(- 6 \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(\pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)}\right) \\ & =\left(- 12 \pi \sin^{2}{\left(\pi t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right)+\left(- 6 \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)} \cos{\left(\pi t \right)}\right) \\ & =- 12 \pi \sin^{2}{\left(\pi t \right)} - 6 \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)} \cos{\left(\pi t \right)} \\ & =- 6 \pi \sin{\left(\pi t \right)} \cos{\left(\pi t \right)} + 6 \pi \cos{\left(2 \pi t \right)} - 6 \pi\end{aligned}

$$

$$
\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm{d}S.
$$

$$

$$
x=2 \cos{\left(t \right)},\quad y=- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)},\quad z=-1
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\langle - 3 z, - 9 x, - 6 y^{2}\rangle \\ & =\langle - 3 \left(-1\right), - 9 \left(2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right), - 6 \left(- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)^{2}\rangle \\ & =\langle 3, - 18 \cos{\left(t \right)}, - 24 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r\prime(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\langle \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right), \frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(-1\right)\rangle \\ & =\langle - 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}, - 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t) & =\langle 3, - 18 \cos{\left(t \right)}, - 24 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\rangle\cdot \langle - 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}, - 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}, 0\rangle \\ & =\left(3\right)\cdot \left(- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 18 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(- 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(- 24 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)\cdot \left(0\right) \\ & =\left(- 6 \sin{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(36 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)+\left(0\right) \\ & =- 6 \sin{\left(t \right)} + 36 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} \\ & =- 6 \sin{\left(t \right)} + 18 \cos{\left(2 t \right)} + 18\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\iint_S\operatorname{curl}F\cdot\mathrm dS & =\oint_C F\cdot\mathrm dr \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi} F(r(t))\cdot r\prime(t)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\left(- 6 \sin{\left(t \right)} + 18 \cos{\left(2 t \right)} + 18\right)\,\mathrm dt \\ & =\left[\left(18 t\right) + \left(6 \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) + \left(9 \sin{\left(2 t \right)}\right)\right]_{0}^{2 \pi} \\ & =\left(\left(36 \pi\right) + \left(6\right) + \left(0\right)\right)-\left(\left(0\right) + \left(6\right) + \left(0\right)\right) \\ & =36 \pi\end{aligned}

$$
